'''Katherine Theresa Stewart Mathieson''' (born 17 August 1975) is the Director of the [[Royal Institution]] and former Chief Executive of the [[British Science Association]]. She previously led the science education projects at [[Nesta (charity)|Nesta]].

== Early life and education ==
Mathieson was born on 17 August 1975 in [[Durham, England|Durham]], the daughter of Martin and Susan Mathieson. She received her BSc in [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences]] from [[Selwyn College, Cambridge]] in 1996. She completed a Masters in [[Science communication|Science Communication]] at [[Imperial College London]] in 1999.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title=Mathieson, Katherine Theresa Stewart, (born 17 Aug. 1975), Chief Executive, British Science Association, since 2016 {{!}} WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-288294|language=en|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U288294|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="Speakers">{{Cite news|url=https://sruk2017.com/speakers/|title=Speakers|date=2015-03-05|work=V INTERNATIONAL SYMPOSIUM SRUK/CERU|access-date=2018-08-31|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901044501/https://sruk2017.com/speakers/|archive-date=2018-09-01|url-status=dead}}</ref> She earned two [[postgraduate diploma]]s, in Information Science from the [[City, University of London|City University of London]] in 2003 and in Voluntary Sector Management from [[Cass Business School]] in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://longitudeprize.org/people/katherine-mathieson|title=Katherine Mathieson {{!}} Longitude Prize|website=longitudeprize.org|language=en|access-date=2018-08-31|archive-date=1 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901003801/https://longitudeprize.org/people/katherine-mathieson|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
Mathieson worked as a GP rep for [[Merck & Co.]] from 1996 to 1998. In 1999, she became a Science Information Officer for Science Line until joining the [[Forensic Science Service]] as an Information Scientist from 2000 to 2002.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.globalbiotechrevolution.com/events/gapsummit-2014/speakers/katherine-mathieson|title=Speakers|last=www.e-mojo.de|first=e-mojo · Multimedia- und Webentwicklung|website=GapSummit 2014 · Global Biotech Revolution|language=en|access-date=2018-08-31|archive-date=1 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901044548/https://www.globalbiotechrevolution.com/events/gapsummit-2014/speakers/katherine-mathieson|url-status=dead}}</ref> Mathieson led science education and enterprise education at [[Nesta (charity)|Nesta]] from 2000.<ref>{{Citation|title=Putting science at the heart of society and culture {{!}} 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160824230040/http://www.iop.org/education/teacher/support/girls_physics/action/file_41603.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> As Director of Education at the [[British Science Association]], Mathieson coordinated outreach activities for school teachers and their students.<ref>{{Cite In 2015 she joined the [[King's College London]] Youth Access and Equity Research and Practice Agenda.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/sspp/departments/education/research/research-centres/crestem/research/current-projects/yaerpa/papers.aspx|title=King's College London - News from Parliament|website=UK Parliament|language=en|access-date=2018-08-31}}</ref> In July 2016 Mathieson took up the role as chief executive of the [[British Science Association]] in July 2016.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.britishscienceassociation.org/news/katherine-mathieson-new-ceo|title=Katherine Mathieson announced as new Chief Exec of the BSA|work=British Science Association|access-date=2018-08-31|language=en|archive-date=1 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901044421/https://www.britishscienceassociation.org/news/katherine-mathieson-new-ceo|url-status=dead}}</ref> At the British Science Association she works to make science as fundamental to society.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://blogs.lse.ac.uk/impactofsocialsciences/2017/11/15/rebranding-science-so-it-is-seen-by-all-people-as-a-fundamental-and-inclusive-part-of-our-society/|title=Rebranding science so it is seen by all people as a fundamental and inclusive part of our society|date=2017-11-15|work=Impact of Social Sciences|access-date=2018-08-31|language=en-US}}</ref> She launched ''Not Just for Scientists'' a campaign that looked for "''ideas from people who would like to contribute to debate about science’s role in society''".<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://notjustforscientists.org/idea/share-spending-power/|title=Share the spending power - Not Just For Scientists|work=Not Just For Scientists|access-date=2018-08-31|language=en-GB}}</ref> In 2017 Mathieson met the [[Duke of York]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.royal.uk/court-circular?text=&mrf=&date%5Bmin%5D%5Bdate%5D=22/01/2017&date%5Bmax%5D%5Bdate%5D=22/01/2018&id=&page=124|title=Court Circular|work=The Royal Family|access-date=2018-08-31|language=en}}</ref> She is worried about the teaching of practical science at schools.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/schools-are-told-to-make-science-go-with-a-bang-6v33b70wz|title=Schools are told to make science go with a bang|last=Education Correspondent|first=Nicola Woolcock|date=2017-08-10|work=[[The Times]]|access-date=2018-08-31|language=en|issn=0140-0460}}</ref> In 2018 she became concerned that [[Brian Cox (physicist)|Brian Cox]] and [[David Attenborough]] did not make science accessible to all of the general public.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://inews.co.uk/news/education/brian-cox-is-too-much-an-expert-science-accessible/|title=Brian Cox is 'too much of an expert' to make science accessible|date=2018-05-17|work=i|access-date=2018-08-31|language=en-GB}}</ref>
